title: A Well for the Smile
premise: Ulyana Okonkwo returns to the family house in Enugu to bury her twin brother Uzo, only to find the body in the casket is wearing her face — and the man calling himself Uzo, alive and insisting she is the one who died, has already signed papers selling the house to a stranger who never blinks. The mirrors lag by a second because something crossed over during the twins' childhood game of 'well,' a dare they made at the dry well behind the house, and it wants a resident before dawn. As neighbors, lawyers, and the buyer converge on the house for the morning signing, Ulyana must uncover which twin actually came back and what their mother traded years ago to keep either of them. At sunrise she signs nothing, names the thing aloud using the truth her brother died protecting, and chooses exile from the family name rather than belonging to what waits below the well.
about_author: Beatrix Oyelaran is a former probate clerk from Ibadan who spent six years cataloguing disputed inheritances before turning to fiction. She writes horror about paperwork, property, and the dead who refuse to be filed away.

chapters.title: The Wrong Face in the Casket
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. She arrives home for Uzo's funeral and finds the corpse wearing her features; the funeral director blames embalming error, but the mourners keep glancing at her like she's the ghost. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as grief curdles into suspicion that someone swapped more than a body.

chapters.title: He Signs with His Left Hand
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. A living 'Uzo' greets her at the gate, calm, left-handed where her brother was right-handed, and produces documents selling the house to a buyer named Mr. Adeyemi, whose reflection arrives slightly after he does. Beat: uncanny wrongness; Ulyana's disbelief becomes her armor and her blind spot.

chapters.title: The Well Game
chapters.summary: POV alternating memories via Ulyana's journal. Flashbacks reveal the twins' childhood dare: whoever leaned over the dry well and smiled longest won, until the night Mother dragged them both inside and burned their shoes. Beat: nostalgia rotting into guilt — the reader learns the well was never empty.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Every mirror in the house now reflects the room a beat behind; in the lag she sees figures standing where no one stands. The lawyer arrives early to 'witness' the sale and refuses to look above her chin. Beat: isolation — the house itself begins testifying against her sanity.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana searching the locked study. She finds her mother's old account book: payments to a well-digger, then entries reading 'one smile, owed' repeated across twenty years, ending the week of the funeral. Beat: revelation — survival was purchased, and the debt has come due to whichever twin remains.

chapters.title: Adeyemi Comes at Dusk
chapters.summary: POV Mr. Adeyemi (brief, cold). He inspects the house at twilight, tests each mirror with a match flame, and tells Ulyana the sale isn't about land: 'I'm buying the resident. You're just deciding which one.' Beat: escalation — the legal machinery revealed as a cover for something older.

chapters.title: Which Twin Came Home
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana confronting 'Uzo' at midnight. Under pressure his face slides between hers and her brother's; he claims she drowned in the well years ago and everything since is the lag. Beat: identity crisis at its peak — the reader doubts Ulyana exactly as she doubts herself.

chapters.title: The Papers on the Table
chapters.summary: POV Ulyana. Neighbors gather for the 6 a.m. signing; the lawyer lays out two deeds, one per twin, and the mirrors all show the room empty except for the table. Ulyana realizes signing anything — even refusing formally — counts as consent. Beat: trap closing; justice outside any court she can appeal to.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Climax, POV Ulyana. She descends to the dry well with the ledger, speaks her mother's original bargain aloud, and offers the debt what it actually asked for: not a body, but the smile — the lie of belonging. The false twin unravels into the well's dark; Adeyemi's contract burns to ash in the first light. Beat: sacrifice and naming as weapons.

chapters.title: No Resident
chapters.summary: Resolution, POV Ulyana. The house sells legitimately to a young family; the mirrors run true. Ulyana leaves under her own name alone, having renounced the inheritance and the town, carrying only the ledger's final page. Beat: bittersweet freedom — she survived by refusing every door that was opened for her, and the price is belonging nowhere at all.
